text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- The offices of a Slovenian organistion in southern Austria were destroyed in an arson attack. The organisation believes the attack was politically motivated.
- The construction industry expects a new boom by the year 2000, while it complains of slow public investments.
- Since Austria Tabak sold sports-goods maker HTM last year, the company has had its best business year.
- After it seemed all sides had agreed on the new laws over shop opening hours, traders and trade unions are criticising plans to let family-owned shops open on Sundays.
- Conservative defence Minister Fasslabend plans to sell army barracks to pay for new tanks. However the Social Democrats have still not agreed to the plans.
- As latest government income figures show, the Finance Ministry's budget plans for 1996 are on course.
- The Austro-Italo-German consortium around EA-Generali wants to speed up the privatisation process for Creditanstalt by reducing complicated contract agreements within the group.
- Pepsi-Cola will move its head office for Eastern Europe from Vienna to Budapest and Moscow from January 1 1997.
- The real estate unit of Creditanstalt Oerag is planning a gradual expansion into the eastern European markets.
- Minimum wages for workers in the paper industry will rise by 2.2 percent from January 1.
- Italy's Finance Minister Carlo Ciampi and Austria's Viktor Klima intend to work together for an EU-wide labour protection and tax system harmonisation.
